rules.title: policymaker, policymaking
rules.text: One word.

rules.title: press secretary
rules.text: Always lowercase.

rules.title: cellphone
rules.text: Lowercase, one word.

rules.title: asylum-seeker
rules.text: A person fleeing their country due to persecution, planning to apply for asylum in the U.S.

rules.title: free-trade agreement
rules.text: Hyphenated in this form.

rules.title: email
rules.text: Do not hyphenate.

rules.title: child care
rules.text: Two words as noun and adjective: *the child care center.*

rules.title: U.S. political parties: Democratic Party
rules.text: Use Democratic, not Democrat, for uses such as *Democratic-controlled Senate* and the *Democratic senator.*

rules.title: canvassing
rules.text: The act of soliciting votes from potential voters.

rules.title: chair
rules.text:
Use instead of *chairwoman* or *chairman.* Capitalize as a title before a person’s name. 

When using chair as a title, remove committee: *House Ways and Means Chair Jason Smith,* not *House Ways and Means Committee Chair Jason Smith.*
terms: house ways and means committee chair

rules.title: startup; start up
rules.text: Use startup as a noun, start up as a verb.

rules.title: front-runner
rules.text: With hyphen.

rules.title: green light, green-light
rules.text:
Use two words as a noun.
>Example: The racer got the green light to start.

Hyphenate the verb. Use green-lighted and not green-lit.
>Example: The studio green-lighted the movie.

rules.title: workday, workforce, workplace, workweek
rules.text: All one word.

rules.title: dataset
rules.text: One word.

rules.title: conspiracy theorist, election denier
rules.text: Avoid using these terms to describe a person. Instead, be more precise about what actions a person is taking, for example, *a person who denies Biden won the 2020 election.*

rules.title: decision-maker, decision-making
rules.text: Hyphenated.

rules.title: co-
rules.text: Use a hyphen for nouns, adjectives and verbs that indicate occupation or status: *co-author, co-chair, co-defendant, co-host, co-pilot, co-star, co-worker*.

rules.title: login, logoff, logon; log in, log off, log on
rules.text:
Use one word in the noun and adjective forms. 
>Example: She forgot her login password.

Use two words in the verb form. 
>Example: Steve forgot to log off.

rules.title: Signalgate
rules.text: One word, lowercase g, no quotation marks. A March 2025 incident that unveiled messages sent between top Trump administration officials through the encrypted messaging app Signal. The group chat included The Atlantic’s editor-in-chief Jeffrey Goldberg, who exposed the messages detailing a planned military strike against the Iran-backed Houthi militant group in Yemen.

rules.title: Congress
rules.text: Capitalize, but lowercase congressional.

rules.title: U.S. representative, representative, member of Congress, lawmaker
rules.text: Use instead of *congressman,* *congresswoman* or *congressperson* when referring to members of the House. Use *senator* or *lawmaker* when referring to members of the Senate.

rules.title: districts
rules.text: Use figures even when the district number is smaller than 10: *1st Congressional District* or *1st District* not *First Congressional District, First District.* When abbreviating, use postal shorthand and add zero to single-digit districts: *NH-01, NY-04.*

rules.title: pre-K
rules.text: Write as pre-K.

rules.title: adviser
rules.text: Use adviser instead of advisor, except when referring to anyone with advisor as an official title.

rules.title: Honorifics
rules.text: Do not use honorifics, *Mr., Mrs., Ms., Miss,* outside of direct quotations or quoted material, and do not use them to distinguish between people with the same last name. Include period if used. Also, see our [entry on Dr.](https://stylebook.politicoapps.com/rule/292ca63a-8900-4589-ace4-b233d06ebd59)

rules.title: POLITICO Pro
rules.text: When referencing in a story, use **POLITICO**, sted POLITICO Pro, Pro, Pro XXXXX: *Boehner told POLITICO* sted *Boehner told POLITICO Pro* or *Boehner told Pro Health Care.* Campaign Pro is the exception.

rules.title: G10
rules.text: The G7 plus Belgium, the Netherlands and Sweden. G10 is acceptable on first reference.

rules.title: interoperability
rules.text: Down in all uses; ability of various technology systems or devices to be able to work together.

rules.title: "Liberation Day"
rules.text: Use quotation marks around "Liberation Day" with an explanation: "Liberation Day," a term coined by the Trump White House, refers to President Donald Trump's April 2, 2025, rollout of reciprocal tariffs on imports from countries his administration identified as having unfair trade surpluses with the U.S. and significant barriers to American goods.

rules.title: first lady
rules.text: Never capitalize first lady as a title: *first lady Melania Trump*.

rules.title: timeframe
rules.text: One word.

rules.title: daylong, dayslong
rules.text: One word.

rules.title: ranking member
rules.text:
Most senior member of a minority party on a congressional or state legislature committee. Down in all instances, even before a name. 
>Example: The witness was questioned by ranking member Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.).

rules.title: down-ballot
rules.text: Refers to races that are below the most important offices listed on an electoral ballot. Note hyphen; not downballot.

rules.title: war chest
rules.text: Avoid using this term. Use *campaign funds* or *in the bank* instead.

rules.title: megadonor
rules.text: Refers to individuals making large donations to a candidate, political party or organization

rules.title: tax exempt, tax-exempt
rules.text:
Two words for the noun. 
>Example: The organization was tax exempt. 

Hyphenate the adjective: 
>The organization checked on its tax-exempt status.

rules.title: hyphens
rules.text: Modifying adverbs ending in -ly are not hyphenated: *widely known*, not *widely-known*.

rules.title: New York state
rules.text: The word state is lowercase.

rules.title: Using gender-neutral language
rules.text: In general, use terms that can apply to any gender.

rules.title: co-pay, co-payment
rules.text: Use a hyphen.

rules.title: web, website, webcast, webpage
rules.text: web, website, webcast, webpage

rules.title: national security adviser
rules.text: Always lowercase title in accordance with AP style.

rules.title: whistleblower
rules.text: Use this term discerningly. A whistleblower is a credible person from inside a company or the government who has firsthand knowledge or documentation of wrongdoing, then makes a disclosure with the reasonable belief that it shows evidence of lawbreaking, misconduct, abuse of power or unethical behavior. A whistleblower can raise concerns internally, make disclosures to an official entity — law enforcement, Congress, an inspector general, etc. — or alert the public, either directly or through journalists. The dozens of whistleblower protection laws at the federal and state level can vary in their definitions, but a common thread is that a whistleblower is someone exercising their First Amendment rights, through lawfully established procedures, to challenge an abuse that betrays the public trust. A whistleblower’s motive can and should be taken into account for assessing their reliability, but the federal Whistleblower Protection Act specifically says it is irrelevant to the protections the person receives. The accuracy and credibility of the information provided is most important.

rules.title: cease fire, ceasefire
rules.text: One word, no hyphen for both the noun and adjective form. Use two words for the verb.

rules.title: JPMorgan Chase
rules.text: Write as JPMorgan Chase.

rules.title: Vance, JD
rules.text: Republican vice president and former senator from Ohio. Do not use periods between J and D. Do not say he grew up in Appalachia, as that is inaccurate. Instead, use southwestern Ohio or a Cincinnati suburb.

rules.title: reelection, reelect
rules.text: These terms are written with no hyphens.

rules.title: cleanup, clean up
rules.text:
Use one word as a noun and adjective. 
>Example: The toxic waste cleanup will take years.

Use two words as a verb. 
>Example: DuPont will clean up the chemical spill.
